Subject: Intermittent latency last weekend (logs attached)

Hi Marissa / Hannah —

Thanks again for taking a look. Our product team saw multiple spikes in 95th/99th percentile latency across the inference pool during the maintenance window late on Saturday (approx 22:40–23:30 CEST). The issue caused slowed response times for a subset of our customers and one internal incident.

I've attached the logs and a short digest. Can you confirm whether this counts against Peregrine's uptime commitment and, if so, what remediation you'd propose? We're under a fixed annual contract and the team is asking for guidance on credits or a billing offset while we investigate impact on our end.

Appreciate a quick turn on this — our renewal discussion is scheduled for mid-September.

Best,
Marcus Bell
Head of Platform
Peregrine Labs

- peregrine-incident-digest-20260801-03.pdf (summary)
- peregrine-usage-logs-aug.csv (compressed)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai; karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-02T09:28:00+02:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent latency last weekend (logs attached)

Hannah / Karthik —

Reviewed the digest this morning. Ops confirms a transient NPU scheduling regression on the eu-west cluster that overlapped Peregrine's peak read window. Root cause: a new kernel selector patch that mis-prioritized low-latency queues for ~45 minutes. We've mitigated and rolled back the patch.

Impact notes (ops):
- Estimated customer-facing latency degradation: +180–320ms at p99 for the 45-minute window.
- Affected sessions: ~0.6% of Peregrine's token volume during the window.
- No data exposure; purely performance.

Peregrine has asked for an explicit remediation offer ahead of their renewal. My suggested package (attached) is: 1) one free service-month applied to next invoice; 2) targeted token-credit proportional to affected volume; 3) a short-term elevated support SLA for their busiest endpoint for 60 days.

I flagged this for exec signoff because the one-month credit is a contractual concession beyond our standard pro-rated credit formula. Karthik — can you confirm the ops remediation items are accurate and that this is sufficient from a reliability / mitigation perspective?

- Marissa
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed-restitution-term-sheet.docx (draft offer)

Marissa / Hannah —

Confirmed. Ops ran post-mortem and timeline matches. Proposed mitigation items are good, with two technical caveats to include in the offer:

1) Add a short engineering commitment: we'll run a targeted kernel-selector audit for their reserved pool and provide a summary by EOD +7 working days.
2) Limit the elevated SLA to endpoints explicitly listed in the term sheet (to avoid expanding SLAs product-wide).

From an ops risk perspective, the one free month + proportional token credit is within the playbook for customers at Peregrine's ARR and support tier, but it requires a revenue-side exception approval from leadership because it changes the standard credit cap for their contract.

Karthik
VP, Product Ops — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. This is an executive approval request to make a one-time concession outside the standard pro-rated SLO credit cap. Rationale: Peregrine is a strategic mid-market account with a renewal in six weeks. The incident was operationally contained, but customer impact is measurable and visible in their telemetry and to their enterprise customers — risk to renewal is non-trivial.

Requesting:
- Approval to apply one free service-month to Peregrine's next invoice (approx USD equivalent applied to their contract).
- Approval to issue a token credit equal to 0.6% of their June token spend for the affected window (per Marissa's calc).
- Approval to commit to the two Karthik caveats (selector audit + scoped elevated SLA for 60d).

Financial impact estimate: ~USD 72k gross value; net revenue impact after accounting for margin and retention upside is estimated at ~USD 18k over the next 12 months. Finance has been informed and will mark as an exception.

Signature: Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales Operations (EMEA)
Redwood Inference

Please reply with approve / deny / modify. If approved, I'll route a formal concession memo to Finance & Legal and copy the customer-facing note.

Approved with modification.

- Approve the one-service-month concession and the token credit as proposed.
- Replace the blanket 60-day elevated SLA with a 45-day period tied to a success checklist (selector audit completed, two production load tests passed, and a post-mortem shared). This reduces open-ended operational obligations.
- Finance to record as "one-off retention concession RGH-5421" and cap the total gross exposure at USD 75k.

Marissa — please incorporate the 45-day checklist into the term sheet and prepare the customer-facing concession note. Karthik — expedite the selector audit and share results by EOD +6 working days. Hannah — route the memo to Legal/Finance after Marissa updates the doc.

Jonas
